artifact.title: Inheritance Conservation Theorem
artifact.statement: Any property inherited from the Universal Entity Model need not be redundantly specified by descendant artifact classes unless explicitly overridden.

tests.name: Duplication Elimination
tests.finding: Common metadata is defined once in the Universal Entity Model.

tests.name: Specification Simplification
tests.finding: Descendant specifications reference inherited properties rather than redefining them.

tests.name: Override Safety
tests.finding: Overrides must be explicit and shall not violate inherited invariants.

tests.name: Forward Compatibility
tests.finding: Adding inherited properties automatically extends descendant entities.

tests.name: Repository Consistency
tests.finding: A single inheritance source reduces divergence across artifacts.

limitations: Inherited properties may only be overridden where the base specification explicitly permits extension.
Identity, provenance, and lifecycle are non-overridable kernel properties.
artifact.conclusion: The theorem is supported as a foundational engineering principle for the AKS Semantic Kernel.
